summary: Every aircraft, including commercial unpiloted aircraft systems, must be registered with WSDOT for each calendar year operated/based in Washington. $15/drone/year, renews annually in January, in addition to FAA registration. Registration via Secure Access Washington (SAW) portal.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Add WSDOT registration and its January renewal to the standard equipment-onboarding and annual-compliance checklist for every drone that will fly in Washington — it's easy to miss because it sits outside the FAA registration workflow most crews already know.
practical_interpretation_agency_practiti: This RCW establishes the registration requirement but is not itself an administering office; the Washington State Legislature does not run a registration or exemption channel. Use WSDOT Aviation Division's actual registration/exemption process (see WA-002) before placing an aircraft on a covered mission, and retain the registration or written exemption determination with the fleet record.

practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: Registration lapses are a straightforward compliance gap to catch in an internal audit; require proof of current WSDOT registration before dispatching any airframe on a Washington job, the same way you'd confirm current insurance and FAA Part 107 currency.

WSDOT UAS Users Manual provides an internal operating-rules model. State UAS Coordinator: Eddy Hensley, eddy.hensley@wsdot.wa.gov, 564-999-1040.

Confirm which aircraft and operator details, fees, renewal dates, and exemption evidence apply to this operation, and retain the registration or written exemption determination with the fleet record.

source_title: Dangerous drone operation near correctional facility — never enacted (2016 Senate Bill 6437)
citation: 2016 Senate Bill 6437 / 1st Substitute SB 6437 (new sections proposed to RCW 72.09 and RCW 9A.76) — died in Senate Rules Committee, never enacted
source_type: Repealed, expired, or superseded authority (never enacted)
status: Not law - died in Senate Rules Committee ("X" file), February 25, 2016; never received a House reading; not enacted
regulated_activity: Myth-busting: no Washington statute currently criminalizes drone operation near a correctional facility
commercial_operator_relevance: High (risk of relying on bad information)
summary: As introduced, 2016 Senate Bill 6437 (1st Substitute) would have added a new RCW 72.09 section directing the Department of Corrections to acquire drone detection/deterrence technology, and a new RCW 9A.76 section making it an unranked Class C felony to knowingly operate a drone over or within 1,000 ft of a correctional facility perimeter without DOC authorization. The Senate Law & Justice Committee reported a substitute bill do-pass on February 5, 2016, and it was placed on second reading by the Rules Committee on February 15, 2016 -- but the Senate Rules Committee "X-filed" the bill on February 25, 2016 (removed it from further consideration), and it was never given a floor vote, never crossed over to the House, and was not enacted. No successor bill accomplishing the same result was identified in a later session. There is currently no Washington statute specifically criminalizing drone operation near a correctional facility; ordinary Washington criminal law (e.g., general trespass, contraband-introduction, and obstruction statutes) may still apply to the underlying conduct the bill targeted, but no UAS-specific correctional-facility offense exists.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: No Washington-specific standoff distance or felony exposure attaches to correctional-facility overflight under this particular (never-enacted) provision. General common-sense coordination with facility staff before flying near a Washington prison is still good practice, but do not plan around a specific 1,000-ft/felony rule -- it was never enacted.
practical_interpretation_uas_procurement: N/A — no procurement or equipment-selection implication identified
practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: Correct this specific point if a client-facing compliance document or training material asserts a Washington drone-correctional-facility felony statute -- it does not exist. If a project genuinely requires flight near a Washington DOC facility, coordinate directly with facility administration as a matter of operational courtesy and safety, not because of this statute, and separately confirm whether general trespass or obstruction law could apply to the specific conduct planned.
verification_status: Verified directly against the Washington State Legislature's own bill-history page (app.leg.wa.gov/billsummary) and the Senate Bill Report: bill history shows Senate Rules "X" file on 2026-08-07 (bill history event dated 2016-02-25), reintroduced-and-retained language for the 2016 1st Special Session (standard procedural carryover, not passage), and no subsequent action of any kind -- no House reading is recorded at all. Corrects the prior pass's Low-confidence 'UNCERTAIN' status, which had not checked the bill's own official history page.
notes: Retrofit 2026-08-07: resolved the prior pass's open high-priority verification item. Retained (like WA-010) as an explicit myth-busting record given the felony-level stakes if a reader mistakenly assumed this bill passed.

source_title: Use of aircraft/unmanned aircraft to pursue, concentrate, or harass wildlife; hunting-day restriction
regulated_activity: Using a UAS to pursue/concentrate/harass wildlife; spotting/locating wildlife by drone for hunting purposes; hunting on the same day a UAS was operated
summary: It is unlawful to use a vehicle, aircraft, unmanned aircraft, or motor-propelled boat to pursue, concentrate, or harass wild animals/birds, except as authorized by WDFW for wildlife-conflict purposes. Separately unlawful to use aircraft (including UAS) to spot/locate/report wildlife location for hunting purposes, and to hunt game animals/birds/migratory birds on the same day one has operated a UAS.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Avoid low-altitude pursuit-like maneuvers near wildlife concentrations on environmental-monitoring and corridor-mapping flights — steady, predictable flight paths at planned survey altitude are unlikely to implicate this rule, but circling or diving near animals could.
practical_interpretation_agency_practiti: If the work is actually part of an agency-directed wildlife-conflict response, contact the Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife before mobilization and ask for the applicable authorization and operating conditions. Ordinary environmental monitoring or mapping does not become authorized wildlife pursuit or harassment merely because it serves a professional purpose, so retain the agency direction and mission limits.
practical_interpretation_uas_procurement: N/A — no procurement or equipment-selection implication identified
practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: Document flight altitude and purpose for any survey work near known wildlife concentrations; the hunting-day restriction is not directly relevant to commercial survey operations but is worth a one-line mention in field-crew orientation for staff who also hunt recreationally in Washington.
verification_status: Verified directly against current WAC rule text

source_title: Operating Unmanned Aircraft on the State Capitol Campus
uas_topic: State capitol campus UAS launch/landing prohibition
regulated_activity: Launching, landing, or operating a UAS on state capitol campus grounds and waters
requirement_type: Prohibition with narrow exclusions and a director-approval pathway
permit_or_approval_required: Yes, for the maintenance/custody exclusion only (director's prior written approval); no permit pathway exists for general commercial use
summary: WAC 200-250-030 closes the entire Washington state capitol campus (Legislative Building, Temple of Justice, Governor's Mansion, 15 state agency office buildings, monuments/memorials, Capitol Lake, and several parks) to launching, landing, or operating any unmanned aircraft, except for the exclusions listed in WAC 200-250-040: emergency law enforcement/fire response; other health-and-human-safety emergency response (search and rescue, health/environmental incidents); national defense activities; and activities necessary for the care and custody of the capitol campus with the Department of Enterprise Services director's prior written approval. WAC 200-250-050 sets out the approval criteria and process for that fourth, narrow exclusion (public-safety impact, damage risk, conflict with the site's historic/commemorative purpose, interference with visitor services, and similar factors) -- it is not a general-purpose commercial-use permit pathway. Violators face a fine or criminal charges; DES coordinates enforcement with the Washington State Patrol and FAA.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Treat the capitol campus as a no-fly zone for launch/landing on any project scope, absent one of the four narrow exclusions -- there is no standard commercial-work permit pathway here, unlike the state parks rule (WA-003). If a project genuinely requires capitol-campus work, budget significant lead time to seek the director's written approval under the maintenance/custody exclusion and expect it to be evaluated case-by-case, not routinely granted.
practical_interpretation_agency_practiti: Contact the Washington Department of Enterprise Services before any capitol-campus-adjacent flight, even for what seems like a minor or brief operation -- the prohibition applies to the entire campus boundary, not just building airspace, and covers recreational and commercial use identically. Do not assume a state-agency client relationship on campus creates an exception.
practical_interpretation_uas_procurement: N/A — no procurement or equipment-selection implication identified
practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: This is a strict-liability-style site prohibition, not a permit-and-comply regime like WA-003 (state parks) -- confirm project scope excludes capitol campus grounds during proposal review, since there is no routine approval path for ordinary commercial AEC work here, and unauthorized operation carries criminal exposure, not just a civil fine.
verification_status: Full current rule text verified directly against the Washington State Legislature's official WAC 200-250 page in this retrofit pass.
notes: New record added in this retrofit pass; not previously captured in this register despite being current, binding, and directly relevant to any capitol-campus-sited AEC work.
